reframe.title: The real question is how to make the tap feel personal
reframe.line: People value water but never link it to their own tap.

claims.text: People value water in the abstract

insight.why: It is the only one that names the tap.
insight.title: People care about water but never see the tap they use

evidence.text: The brief names the gap between caring and connecting.

audience.title: Households who never think about the tap
audience.primary: Adults 25 to 54 in the Lumen Water region.

rtbs.text: Lumen Water has served the region for 40 years

from_to.to: Water is something I look after

insight_candidates.observation: People say they care about water, yet turn the tap on without a thought.
insight_candidates.tension: But the care lives in the abstract and the tap they use is invisible to them.
insight_candidates.implication: So make the tap the place where the care shows up.
insight_candidates.not_in_brief: The care and the habit never meet at the tap.
insight_candidates.swap_test: A phone company could not say this: it is about a tap.

insight_candidates.observation: People notice water only when the bill lands.
insight_candidates.tension: But a bill makes water a cost, while nobody feels it as a thing they look after.
insight_candidates.implication: So give people a moment of looking after water before the bill.
insight_candidates.not_in_brief: The bill is the only touchpoint.

insight_candidates.observation: The category promises clean water and delivers a bill.
insight_candidates.tension: Yet nobody believes a utility is on their side.
insight_candidates.implication: So show the utility as a neighbour.
